paper_metadata.title: Train-and-Scaling the Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz to Solve Portfolio Diversification

experiments.description: Train-and-Scale QAOA applied to portfolio diversification instances mapped to Maximum Independent Set on SP500-derived correlation graphs, evaluated across increasing subgraph sizes from n=6 to n=30 with depth grown iteratively.

algorithm.variant: Train-and-Scale QAOA for MIS/portfolio diversification with iterative depth growth and warm-start retraining
algorithm.optimizer: parameter-shift-based gradient descent with random parameter selection
algorithm.num_layers: p grows from pmin=6 up to p=54 for n=30; depth increased by 2 per size in reported results
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Warm-start from previously trained smaller-instance parameters; new layer inserted with zero initialization

optimizer_settings.learning_rate_schedule: exponential decay from 0.02 to 0.002 over 64 epochs
optimizer_settings.parameter_sampling: select a parameter uniformly at random

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One binary variable per graph vertex/asset; graph edges defined by correlation thresholding of SP500 covariance/correlation matrix
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximum Independent Set: minimize sum_i (1 - x_i) subject to x_i x_j = 0 for all edges (v_i, v_j) in E
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Constrained QAOA mixer that preserves the independent-set subspace via an irreducibly commuting mixer
problem_formulation.num_binary_variables: n, equal to the number of vertices/assets in each graph instance
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Embedded constraint operator C_mis = sum_(v_i,v_j in E) sigma1_i sigma1_j; cost Hamiltonian H_c = sum_i sigma0_i

problem_instance.description: SP500 stock portfolio diversification instances generated from monthly correlation graphs; subgraphs of varying size extracted by breadth-first search around a randomly selected starting node
problem_instance.num_assets: Between 6 and 30 for the main Train-and-Scale evaluation; underlying monthly dataset contains between 350 and 500 stocks
problem_instance.time_steps: Daily prices within each month; monthly windows from 2010 to 2020
problem_instance.dataset_size: 500 graphs per size for sizes 6 to 100 in the generated training sets; main reported evaluation focuses on sizes 6 to 30

preprocessing: compute sample covariance and Pearson correlation between assets
threshold absolute correlation at lambda to form unweighted graph
generate subgraphs by breadth-first search around a randomly selected starting node

quantum_resources.num_qubits: n, equal to the number of graph vertices/assets in each instance
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: p, scaled up to 54 for n=30

classical_preprocessing: construct monthly correlation graphs from SP500 returns
generate size-n subgraphs via breadth-first search
randomized partitioning of mixer generators into commuting groups
classical_postprocessing: estimate success probability / inverse success probability

speedup_claims.conditions: QAOA-54 on correlation graphs from n=6 to n=100, lambda=0.1
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an empirical comparison of fitted scaling exponents, not a proven asymptotic speedup.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial scaling in depth and sampling complexity
speedup_claims.conditions: if the observed trend continues to hundreds of variables
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this as a possibility, not a proven result.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not explicitly stated; empirical scaling reported as p = O(n) and sampling complexity exponent 0.044 for QAOA-54 on n up to 100
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Not explicitly stated; simulated annealing baseline used empirically
